audits.title: 511 An Audit on the Use of a Calibration Marker in Neck of Femur Fracture X Rays
audits.standard: NICE: calibration marker on all X-rays for possible neck of femur fracture
audits.setting: Major trauma centre (Royal Victoria Infirmary, Newcastle)

cycle1.result: Previous QIP improved compliance from 64% to 73%.

cycle2.result: Only 44% had a ball calibration marker on the original X-ray.

audits.other_findings: Compliance fell after the first loop; re-audit planned.
audits.citation: Rao C, Altahoo H, Anjum S, Martin R, Critchley R, Chambers S. 511 An Audit on the Use of a Calibration Marker in Neck of Femur Fracture X Rays. British Journal of Surgery. 2025;112(Supplement_10). doi:10.1093/bjs/znaf128.691.

audits.title: IMPROVING STANDARDS OF LONG LEG ALIGNMENT RADIOGRAPHS AT A UK DISTRICT GENERAL HOSPITAL: A QUALITY IMPROVEMENT PROJECT
audits.standard: Locally defined standard: blocks under the shorter limb where there is clear leg length discrepancy, equal pelvic height and patella facing forwards
audits.setting: UK district general hospital, Maidstone & Tunbridge Wells NHS Trust, patients under 18

cycle1.result: 116/243 (48%) performed with patella facing forwards; of 110 patients needing blocks, none had them used.

audits.other_findings: 133/243 radiographs were for reasons other than leg length discrepancy.
audits.citation: Bishop N, Green G, Firth G, Hong Tang C, Dartnell J, Katchburian M. IMPROVING STANDARDS OF LONG LEG ALIGNMENT RADIOGRAPHS AT A UK DISTRICT GENERAL HOSPITAL: A QUALITY IMPROVEMENT PROJECT. Orthopaedic Proceedings. 2025;107-B(SUPP_3):42-42. doi:10.1302/1358-992x.2025.3.042.

audits.title: Retrospective Review of Arthroplasty Radiographs: How to Define an Adequate Radiograph.
audits.standard: Local consensus criteria (seven arthroplasty and three radiology consultants): nine criteria for adequate post-operative hip and knee arthroplasty radiographs, four essential
audits.setting: Single centre orthopaedic and radiology departments (Leeds Teaching Hospitals affiliation)

cycle1.result: 69/100 radiographs adequate overall; whole prosthesis and cement visible 86%, relevant anatomy visible 83%, pubic symphysis centred 31%, GT/LT level 32%.

audits.intervention: Local guidelines published with radiology, educational and feedback meetings with radiographers, poster in radiography rooms and a quality improvement proforma.

cycle2.result: 84/100 adequate overall; prosthesis and cement visible 93%, relevant anatomy 95%, pubic symphysis centred 47%, GT/LT level 43%; 11/56 (19.6%) hip and 5/44 (11.4%) knee radiographs inadequate.

audits.other_findings: Pain score, BMI and number of radiographers were not correlated with inadequate radiographs; exposure fell slightly (95% to 92%).
audits.citation: Faraz A, Al-Ashqar M, Khan S, Zaman Q, Smyth J, Parker J, et al.. Retrospective Review of Arthroplasty Radiographs: How to Define an Adequate Radiograph. Cureus. 2022;14(7):e26697. doi:10.7759/cureus.26697. PMID: 35959189.

audits.title: The current standard of the shoulder trauma series in Ireland - A national audit.
audits.standard: Pre-defined audit criteria for AP and axillary/Velpeau views
audits.setting: Emergency departments, national audit of public trauma hospitals

cycle1.result: Two views in 75.92% (n = 599); axillary or Velpeau view in 21.17% (n = 167); AP view met audit criteria in 23.09% (n = 181).

audits.other_findings: Surgeon survey (70.8% response): 88.2% favoured three views and 94% a national protocol.
audits.citation: Mc Colgan R, O'Halloran AS, Carroll PJ, Kaar K, O'Shea K. The current standard of the shoulder trauma series in Ireland - A national audit. Surgeon. 2024;22(5):e159-e163. doi:10.1016/j.surge.2024.04.009. PMID: 38677960.

audits.title: Preoperative Templating Prior to Total Hip Arthroplasty: A Closed-Loop Audit.
audits.standard: Templating radiographs 7–180 days before THA (New Zealand Orthopaedic Association, South African Arthroplasty Society and GIRFT guidance); goal 100%
audits.setting: Elective arthroplasty service, Tallaght University Hospital, Dublin

cycle1.result: 10/50 (20%) had templating radiographs within 7–180 days; mean 140 days (range 0–788) from latest radiograph to surgery.

audits.intervention: Departmental protocol requiring preoperative assessment with templating radiographs, education of NCHDs on radiographs to order, and a departmental rota assigning NCHDs to order them.
audits.other_findings: Mean leg length change of 2.26 mm (range 0–17 mm) between radiographs a mean 386 days apart.
audits.citation: Kilkenny CJ, O'Driscoll C, Jassim S, Davey MS, McGoldrick NP, Quinlan JF. Preoperative Templating Prior to Total Hip Arthroplasty: A Closed-Loop Audit. Cureus. 2025;17(1):e77083. doi:10.7759/cureus.77083. PMID: 39917097.

audits.title: Adequacy of Lateral Ankle Radiograph Views in Acute Trauma Setting: A Quality Improvement Project.
audits.standard: BOAST and radiographic positioning criteria for a true lateral ankle view (four criteria); target 100% for each
audits.setting: Trauma unit, district general hospital (University Hospitals Dorset, Poole)

cycle1.result: Criterion 1 (fibula superimposed by posterior tibia) 83%; criterion 2 (talar domes superimposed) 61%; criterion 3 (open uniform tibiotalar joint) 69%; criterion 4 (landmarks included) 99%.

audits.intervention: Posters in the emergency department and orthopaedic on-call room/radiography suites, and a teaching session by a foot and ankle associate specialist for orthopaedic staff and radiographers.
audits.other_findings: Talar dome superimposition remained the hardest criterion to meet; the usual failure of criterion 4 was omission of the base of the fifth metatarsal.
audits.citation: Imtiaz H, Rahim A, Paracha H, Samad S, Kouklidis G, Raymond A. Adequacy of Lateral Ankle Radiograph Views in Acute Trauma Setting: A Quality Improvement Project. Cureus. 2025;17(9):e91479. doi:10.7759/cureus.91479. PMID: 41049922.

audits.title: Assessing Adequacy of Marker Ball Placement in Preoperative Pelvic X-rays: Are We Missing the Mark?
audits.standard: Local trauma unit guideline: marker ball entirely visible and placed between the femurs inferior to the symphysis pubis; agreed target 80% for each
audits.setting: Poole General Hospital trauma unit (district general hospital); AP pelvic radiographs for intracapsular neck of femur fractures

cycle1.result: Marker ball present in 27 (45%). Of these, entirely visible 16 (59%) and correctly positioned 11 (41%); overall compliance 59% (n=16).

audits.intervention: Poster reminders in radiography areas, a presentation to the radiography team by a T&O registrar, and a mandatory checklist for all such X-rays.

cycle2.result: Marker ball present in 39 (78%). Entirely visible 33 (84%, p=0.042) and correctly positioned 32 (82%, p=0.0014); overall compliance 80% (n=31, p=0.132), meeting the target.

audits.other_findings: The methods state the first cycle was completed in June 2025, overlapping the re-audit dates given in the abstract. No inter-observer reliability testing was done.
audits.citation: Rahim AK, Imtiaz H, Afzal I, Karim A, Shah P, Barot K, et al.. Assessing Adequacy of Marker Ball Placement in Preoperative Pelvic X-rays: Are We Missing the Mark?. Cureus. 2025;17(10):e94736. doi:10.7759/cureus.94736. PMID: 41113895.

audits.title: Improving the Quality of Lateral Wrist Radiographs: A Closed-Loop Audit of Radiographic Compliance With Standard Positioning Criteria.
audits.standard: Clark's Positioning in Radiography criteria for lateral wrist radiographs (styloid superimposition, anatomical inclusion, piso-scapho-capitate relationship); target 80% for each
audits.setting: Poole Hospital, district general hospital (University Hospitals Dorset)

cycle1.result: Styloid superimposition 72% (36/50); anatomical inclusion 98% (49/50); piso-scapho-capitate relationship 50% (25/50).

audits.intervention: Poster on positioning technique in the radiology department and trauma meeting rooms, and a formal teaching session by an associate specialist hand surgeon for radiographers and orthopaedic doctors.

cycle2.result: Styloid superimposition 92% (46/50) (p = 0.047); anatomical inclusion 100% (50/50) (p = 0.992); piso-scapho-capitate relationship 82% (41/50) (p = 0.014).

audits.other_findings: All three standards met the 80% target at re-audit; the study did not assess whether any injuries were missed.
audits.citation: Barot K, Rahim AK, Afzal I, Imtiaz H, Kouklidis G, Ahmed T, et al.. Improving the Quality of Lateral Wrist Radiographs: A Closed-Loop Audit of Radiographic Compliance With Standard Positioning Criteria. Cureus. 2025;17(12):e100459. doi:10.7759/cureus.100459. PMID: 41487762.

audits.title: Quality improvement in radiography in a neonatal intensive care unit.
audits.standard: Standards defined a priori for radiographic technique and essential clinical information on X-ray requisitions
audits.setting: Tertiary neonatal intensive care unit, McMaster University, Hamilton

cycle1.result: Baseline review of all neonatal X-rays and requisitions identified areas of suboptimal image quality and documentation (figures not given in abstract).

audits.intervention: Brief educational sessions and printed pamphlets targeting suboptimal areas, delivered jointly by radiology and neonatology staff.

cycle2.result: Improvements in requisition completion and image quality, including legibility (P = 0.019) and completeness of medical history.

audits.other_findings: A re-audit at 1 month (n = 93) also showed improvement; gains were sustained at 1 year.
audits.citation: Loovere L, Boyle EM, Blatz S, Bowslaugh M, Kereliuk M, Paes B. Quality improvement in radiography in a neonatal intensive care unit. Can Assoc Radiol J. 2008;59(4):197-202. PMID: 19069604.

audits.title: Retrospective quality assurance audit of Lateral Cephalometric Radiographs at postgraduate teaching hospital.
audits.standard: National Radiation Protection Board quality grading standards; Royal College of Surgeons of England criteria
audits.setting: Riphah International University postgraduate dental teaching hospital

cycle1.result: 31 Grade I, 16 Grade II and 3 Grade III; only one Royal College criterion (correct head positioning) met the 100% standard.

audits.intervention: Recommendations made for comprehensive radiation protection regulations (no re-audit reported).
audits.other_findings: Errors included poor visibility of soft tissue (16%), teeth not occluded (14%), incorrect label positioning (12%) and sella and nasion not visible (8%).
audits.citation: Khan A, Javed MQ, Bilal R, Gaikwad RN. Retrospective quality assurance audit of Lateral Cephalometric Radiographs at postgraduate teaching hospital. Pak J Med Sci. 2020;36(7):1601-1606. doi:10.12669/pjms.36.7.2796. PMID: 33235582.
